intro: M. Arthur “Art” Gensler Jr. co-founded the design firm Gensler with Drue Gensler and James Follett. The company’s history presents the practice as a collaborative enterprise from its beginning in San Francisco in 1965. Its memorial and leadership history distinguish Art’s founding role from the people who subsequently led the organization.

sections.title: Three founders in a small practice
sections.text: Gensler’s leadership history names Art, Drue and Follett as the co-founders and describes a one-room San Francisco office. It characterizes the early practice around workplace and interior design. The original corporate name appears in the company history as M. Arthur Gensler Jr. & Associates. Retaining all three names is important when a firm’s public brand uses only one founder’s surname.

sections.title: A professional practice with a shared structure
sections.text: The company histories discuss a model built around collaboration, client work and developing leaders across offices. These are the firm’s explanations of its organizational approach. They provide useful professional-service context, but they are not independent evidence that any particular design engagement will follow a uniform process or achieve a specified outcome.

sections.title: The founder’s life and later leadership are distinct
sections.text: Gensler’s memorial identifies Art’s death in 2021 and discusses his withdrawal from executive roles before that. The separate leadership history names subsequent generations of leadership. This entry therefore uses a historical co-founder label and does not assign Art a present management responsibility.

sections.title: Use the biography to understand a practice, not approve a design
sections.text: A client selecting a design team needs project-specific qualifications, scope, responsibilities and evidence relevant to the proposed work. A founder’s reputation or a firm’s historical culture cannot replace that review. This profile evaluates neither design quality nor professional suitability, and makes no inference about current ownership, revenue or personal wealth.

name: David MacNeil
role: Founder and CEO in WeatherTech’s company account reviewed November 21, 2026.
founding: WeatherTech dates its beginning in Clarendon Hills, Illinois, to 1989.
intro: David MacNeil founded WeatherTech in 1989, according to the company’s account. The business is associated with automotive accessories and Illinois manufacturing. Its history distinguishes an early period of importing floor mats from later production changes, making the chronology more specific than a broad claim that every stage began with domestic manufacturing.

sections.title: The early product problem in the company story
sections.text: WeatherTech says MacNeil started the business from his home in Clarendon Hills after dissatisfaction with existing automotive floor mats. The account describes importing mats from England in the early period. This is the company’s explanation of the opportunity it pursued, rather than an independent comparison of product quality.

sections.title: A later change in production
sections.text: The same account dates a move of production to the United States to 2007. MacNeil’s signed 2010 note discusses manufacturing equipment, tooling and materials associated with that approach. This separates the account of product sourcing from the later manufacturing decision. Keeping 1989 and 2007 separate avoids presenting a later production strategy as though it were the complete original operating model.

sections.title: A founder’s stated manufacturing priorities
sections.text: The signed note explains MacNeil’s preference for investing in manufacturing and suppliers closer to the company’s operations. It is useful as first-person evidence of his priorities at that time. Its claims about efficiency and product quality remain attributed statements, not conclusions independently reached by this directory.

sections.title: A product decision still requires current evidence
sections.text: A buyer should confirm the fit, materials, instructions and warranty terms for the exact product being considered. A founder biography cannot establish those particulars for every item in a catalog. This profile uses the company’s founder-and-CEO identification but does not adopt its ownership-percentage claim, estimate personal wealth or evaluate financial performance.

checks: Separate the 1989 start from the 2007 production change.

name: James Henry Ryan
role: Historical founder, as described in company-participant case studies.
founding: The cited participant accounts date Ryan Lumber and Coal in Hibbing, Minnesota, to 1938.
intro: James Henry Ryan founded the lumber-and-coal business associated with today’s Ryan Companies. Direct company-participant accounts published by software supplier Procore describe the early operation and later move into real estate. The current company overview corroborates the 1938 starting year while describing a substantially broader contemporary service business.

sections.title: A lumber-and-coal origin
sections.text: Procore’s Ryan Companies case study says James Henry Ryan and his sons Francis and Russell began Ryan Lumber and Coal in Hibbing in 1938. Because the document features company participants, it is treated here as their account published by a supplier, not as an independent historical investigation. The sons’ involvement remains part of the founding context.

sections.title: A later real-estate chapter
sections.text: A second Procore participant case study describes Francis and Russell assessing the business’s real-estate holdings and developing Ryan Realty Company in 1949. This is a later stage than the original lumber-and-coal operation. The distinction prevents the modern development business from being projected unchanged onto 1938.

sections.title: The current company overview supplies context
sections.text: Ryan’s own About page identifies 1938 as its starting point and describes development, design, engineering, construction and management services. That corroborates the broad chronology without independently proving every anecdote in the supplier case studies. Source type matters when building a biography from several public accounts. Supplier involvement alone does not make every quoted statement independently verified.

sections.title: Keep historical evidence and project evidence separate
sections.text: The founder story can explain how a company describes its development, but it cannot establish current project capability or contract terms. A reader considering an engagement should identify the proposed service and responsible team directly. This profile makes no claim about revenue, family wealth, ownership percentages or the results of any particular development.

checks: Attribute supplier-published history to company participants.

name: Ty Measom
role: Historical founder; the selected 2012 and 2019 documents do not establish a current executive role or ownership interest.
founding: A 2012 filed biography and Camp Chef’s 2019 submission date the business to 1990.
intro: Ty Measom founded Camp Chef in 1990, according to a filed biography and the company’s later government submission. The documents connect the business with outdoor cooking equipment and Logan, Utah. They are historical sources: titles and ownership statements appearing in them should not be treated as automatically current in November 2026.

sections.title: A filed professional biography
sections.text: A 2012 SEC-filed proxy document identifies Measom’s engineering background and says he founded Camp Chef Outdoor Cooking Products in 1990. It places the company in Logan, Utah. The biography’s descriptions of his office and ownership belong to that filing period, not to an independently verified present-day status.

sections.title: The company’s explanation of its first product
sections.text: In a 2019 submission published through Regulations.gov, Camp Chef describes Measom designing a portable stove in response to limitations he saw in outdoor cooking equipment. The document explains the company’s view of the product’s development. This profile does not adopt its comparative safety or performance claims as tested conclusions.

sections.title: A founder speaking about the business
sections.text: Utah State University’s business school published a direct Measom interview in 2017. Its description connects the founding with his work as an engineer and discusses the development of the company’s outdoor cooking range. This offers another dated, directly involved source without establishing that the same product lineup or management arrangements continue today.

sections.title: Treat each source according to its date and purpose
sections.text: A proxy biography, a company submission and an interview were created for different audiences. Together they support a founder association and broad chronology, but they do not amount to a current ownership audit. A product purchase requires current specifications and instructions. This entry does not infer wealth, revenue, current executive authority or the suitability of equipment for a particular use.
